exercise.name: Dumbbell Overhead Lunge

reference.title: Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Lunge
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Thighs, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip, knee and ankle; shoulder held overhead)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as you step forward and lower, exhale as you push back to standing; keep the ribs down.
breathing.cadence: About 1.6 s step and lower, short pause, about 1.7 s push back

prescription.tempo: Controlled step, 1-2 s down, push back in about 1 s
prescription.progression: Heavier dumbbell, then walking overhead lunges. Use a light dumbbell first; the overhead hold, not the legs, limits the load. Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight that leaves about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8) at the end of each set.

cues.text: Press one dumbbell straight overhead, elbow locked, biceps by the ear; free hand on the hip. Stand tall, ribs down.
Take a long step forward and land heel first; the dumbbell stays stacked over the shoulder.
Breathe in and lower the back knee toward the floor; trunk tall, arm vertical.
Breathe out and push off the front foot to step back to standing.
Stand tall and reset; switch the arm and leg on the next set.

mistakes.mistake: Arm drifting forward of the head
mistakes.fix: Keep the dumbbell stacked over the shoulder and the hip; look straight ahead.
Lock the elbow and reach up; use a lighter dumbbell.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back or leaning away from the dumbbell
mistakes.fix: Brace the ribs down and keep the shoulders level.
Keep the front knee over the 2nd-3rd toe.

kinematics.peak: 80 cm forward (72.2 cm between ankle centres once the back heel is up)
kinematics.norm: Front knee about over the front foot at the bottom (common guideline); about one leg length was suggested in the split squat (Song 2023)
About 90 degrees at the bottom (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: ≈102°, 14 cm above the floor (knee joint centre)
kinematics.norm: Lowers to just above the floor (clinical opinion)
Upright: the overhead arm needs a vertical trunk (clinical opinion); more lean shifts work to the hip extensors (Farrokhi 2008)

kinematics.setup: Wrist 1.2° from vertical over the shoulder, elbow ≈12°
kinematics.peak: ≈1.1° from vertical at the bottom (the arm stays vertical in the world)
kinematics.norm: Vertical over the shoulder, elbow locked (clinical opinion)

kinematics.peak: Step 0.8 s, 1.0 s down, 0.3 s pause, 0.75 s up, step back 0.85 s
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 1-2 s down and 1 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #509512, Dumbbell Single Arm Overhead Lunge, video (movement reference)
López-de-Celis, Labata-Lezaun et al. 2023, effect of load distribution on trunk muscle activity with lunge exercises in amateur athletes (Healthcare 11(6):916)
Aspe & Swinton 2014, electromyographic and kinetic comparison of the back squat and overhead squat (J Strength Cond Res 28(10):2827-2836)
Farrokhi et al. 2008, trunk position influences lead-leg kinematics, kinetics and muscle activity in the forward lunge (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 38:403-409)
Song et al. 2023, effects of step lengths on lower-extremity biomechanics during the split squat (Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1277493)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or giving-way occurs.
Choose a dumbbell load you can control for every rep; the load is user-chosen.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Only lunge with a dumbbell you can hold locked overhead; if the arm bends or drifts, lower the dumbbell to the shoulder.
Skip the overhead hold if you have shoulder pain lifting the arm.
modify: Shoulder limits: hold the dumbbell at the shoulder (front rack) instead.
Balance concerns: static split squat with the dumbbell overhead.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Front-leg knee extensors brake the step and drive the push back.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Front-leg hip extensor; hip moments were greater in the forward lunge than in the reverse lunge (PMC4641539).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus assists hip extension and steadies the thigh.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Assist hip extension and co-contract around the front knee.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.calves_l: Steady the front shin; the back calf holds the heel up.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow base with the load on one side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Keeps the pelvis level on the narrow base with the load on one side (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down under the overhead load; overhead squats raised anterior trunk activity only slightly (about 2-7%) over back squats (Aspe 2014).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: With a one-sided load, trunk muscles on the side opposite the dumbbell work harder (López-de-Celis 2023, dumbbell held at the side).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: With a one-sided load, trunk muscles on the side opposite the dumbbell work harder (López-de-Celis 2023, dumbbell held at the side).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the trunk tall; erector spinae activity differed between sides with a one-sided load (López-de-Celis 2023).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the trunk tall; erector spinae activity differed between sides with a one-sided load (López-de-Celis 2023).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Holds the arm straight up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Holds the arm straight up (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the arm up beside the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Holds the arm up beside the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Lift and rotate the shoulder blade to support the arm overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Lift and rotate the shoulder blade to support the arm overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade upward under the overhead load (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blade upward under the overhead load (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the dumbbell handles; the hands stay closed all set (clinical opinion).
